summary: Staggered probe 'timewarp' caused canary traffic diversion and temporary model unpin for customer
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled weighted canary cutover for NovaWriter's dedicated pool, intermittent health probe scheduling jitter (internal name: "probe timewarp") caused the canary-coordinator to observe a temporary unhealthy state for a small cohort of nodes. The orchestrator responded by diverting a subset of tenant traffic to the fallback variant and the edge returned responses from the older version despite the tenant having an active model pin.

Impact:
- Duration: ~18 minutes (2026-03-10 14:02 UTC -> 14:20 UTC)
- Customer-visible: NovaWriter reported ~6% of requests routed to legacy variant, causing content quality regressions and a billing delta due to fallback pricing.
- Affected: single dedicated tenant (NovaWriter) pinned to rw-text-2b-v3; small percent of sessions saw mixed-model outputs.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-novawriter-03 (us-east-1)
- Orchestrator version: v1.14.2
- Canary coordinator: v0.9.7
- Edge-proxy: env prod-edge-12

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Trigger weighted canary from 0% -> 10% for rw-text-2b-v3 at 14:00 UTC (automated rollout).
2) Canary prewarm probes started across 12 nodes (staggered window to avoid thundering herd).
3) Due to a clock skew between probe scheduler and the canary health aggregator (rare scheduling jitter), some probes were delayed by 2x their intended interval leading to transient failing probe counts.
4) Canary coordinator's health smoothing logic interpreted the transient failures as an increasing unhealthy trend and evicted the small cohort from primary selection at ~14:02 UTC.
5) Edge routing layer, upon receiving the orchestrator's updated snapshot, routed some persistent session tokens to fallback variant for 12-18 minutes until reconciliation at 14:20 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- Mixed model outputs for affected sessions (v2 responses interleaved with legacy v1 content).
- Edge logs show routing-change events aligned to orchestrator snapshot commits at 14:02 UTC.
- Canary coordinator metrics show spike in probe-latency and probe-miss counts between 14:01-14:05 UTC.

Expected behavior:
- Transient probe scheduling jitter should be smoothed by the coordinator without evicting cohorts while prewarm window is within allowed jitter tolerance.
- Tenant pin must remain authoritative; temporary health fluctuations should not override explicit pins.

Logs and links:
- Edge event stream excerpt: https://logs.redwood.ai/edge/streams/novawriter/2026-03-10/14
- Canary metrics dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Canary/novawriter-prewarm?from=2026-03-10T13:50:00Z&to=2026-03-10T14:30:00Z
- Orchestrator snapshot commits: https://git.internal/redwood/orchestrator/commits/ae3b7c

Notes for on-call: please preserve logs for the 14:00-14:25 UTC window and tag traces with trace_id starting with nw-14mar.
comments: Aisha Kaur - 2026-03-10: Customer reported at 14:18 UTC that ~6% of their requests returned legacy model outputs during rollout. Collected request IDs and session tokens. Escalating to SRE and Orchestrator team.

Miguel Ortega (SRE) - 2026-03-10: Dug into orchestrator snapshots. Found commit ae3b7c that included a change to probe scheduling backoff. There's a small window where staggered timers can align poorly. Adding @Jordan Lee for canary-coordinator context.

Jordan Lee (Canary Team) - 2026-03-10: Canary coordinator smoothing config is at default (alpha smoothing=3, window=30s). The delayed probes caused temporary unhealthy count increments; coordinator considered cohort degraded because prewarm state machine expects steady probe cadence. We can reproduce in staging with injected timer jitter.

NovaWriter (customer) - 2026-03-10: Impacting content A/B quality in production during launch traffic spike. Need assurance this won't happen on future cutovers. Asked for rollback timestamp and compensation guidance.
Miguel Ortega - 2026-03-11: Applied temporary mitigation on orchestrator (reverted backoff change) and increased coordinator smoothing thresholds for dp-novawriter-03. Monitoring for recurrence.
investigation_notes: 01) Root cause hypothesis: a scheduling backoff adjustment in orchestrator introduced non-uniform probe offsets under certain CPU scheduling conditions, amplifying natural jitter.
02) Repro: deterministically reproduced in staging by injecting 150-250ms probe delay on 3/12 runs; reproduced the cohort eviction behavior after 2 of 5 probes missed inside the smoothing window.
03) Impact assessment: only dedicated pool dp-novawriter-03 with pinned sessions experienced cross-variant routing; global routing and other dedicated pools unaffected.
04) Short-term mitigation: revert recent backoff commit in orchestrator and bump canary smoothing alpha for the tenant. This was applied at 2026-03-11 09:30 UTC.

05) Next steps: patch orchestrator to add probe-sequence-monotonicity guard and update canary coordinator to treat explicit tenant pins as higher priority than transient health evictions. Add e2e test that simulates probe jitter during prewarm.
workaround: Reverted the orchestrator probe backoff change for dp-novawriter-03 and temporarily increased canary coordinator smoothing; customer traffic returned to pinned variant within 18 minutes. Recommended NovaWriter pause any further cutovers for 48 hours.
resolution: In Progress - mitigation applied. Engineering to ship a small orchestrator patch (PR linked) and a coordinator change to honor explicit tenant pins over prewarm health transient states. Targeting full fix in v1.14.4 rollout scheduled 2026-03-18.
follow_up_actions: Create e2e test that injects probe jitter during prewarm and asserts tenant pin dominance (owner: Canary Team, due: 2026-03-15)
Ship orchestrator patch to add probe monotonicity guard (owner: Orchestrator Team, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/2419)
Update runbook: add a section for "probe timewarp" and emergency smoothing adjustments (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-14)
Compensation review with finance for any billing delta reported by NovaWriter (owner: CS Ops, due: 2026-03-13)
